content.text:
Finding submitted.

**Classification: deviation (fallback target)**

- **Customer side (§ 11.1, p0187):** a convenience right exists, but on **one year's notice** plus a Termination for Convenience Fee equal to a percentage of **Estimated Remaining Value** (all remaining months of fees), *plus* unamortized Conversion costs and disposition Expenses, 50% payable on notice and expressly outside the § 13.4 cap — on an eight-year Term (p0049) this fails the fallback's 60–90 days / three-month fee ceiling.
- **M&I side (§ 10.2, p0180):** unilateral withdrawal of any non-Core Service **"at any time"** on 90 days' notice — a mid-term partial convenience right. Notice period already meets the 90-day floor, so only the timing was restricted to the end of the Term.
- **Redline (3 surgical replaces, ok:true):** 90 days' notice; fee capped at three months' average monthly Fees; fee stated as Customer's sole termination payment obligation (removing the add-on costs); M&I withdrawal limited to the end of the Term.
- **Why fallback, not preferred:** deleting the fee entirely would require collateral rewrites to the 50/50 payment mechanic, § 11.2(A) cross-reference and the § 13.5 liquidated-damages acknowledgement. Favourable terms preserved: § 11.2(B) (no fee on M&I default) and § 20.3 (penalty-free Disaster exit); § 2.2 non-renewal left to the RENEWAL rule.
